boards.title: Your First Weekend at Harvard University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A Friday-to-Sunday sequence for learning the campus, sharing first-year meals, finding study spaces, and exploring free public art and history.

cards.entity_name: Richard A. and Susan F. Smith Campus Center
cards.title: Friday: Find Your Starting Point
cards.subtitle: Begin across from Harvard Yard
cards.notes: Step into the Welcome Pavilion, locate the Visitor Center, and use the open seating to compare weekend plans with your group.
cards.short_summary: A practical first stop for orientation, seating, and visitor information.
cards.evidence_claim: The Smith Campus Center stands across from Harvard Yard and provides three floors of open seating and study spaces.
cards.access_notes: Public and Harvard-affiliate access varies by floor; consult posted building access information when entering.

cards.title: Friday: Learn the Square
cards.subtitle: Trace the district beside Harvard Yard
cards.notes: Walk the pedestrian-oriented district, identify the Red Line entrance, and note the bus connections for later trips around Cambridge.
cards.short_summary: A transit-and-navigation loop through the commercial district adjoining campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Cambridge describes Harvard Square as a pedestrian-friendly district centered on a Red Line station with nearby bus connections.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor public district; individual businesses maintain separate access policies and schedules.

cards.title: Friday: Share a First-Year Dinner
cards.subtitle: Meet inside Memorial Hall
cards.notes: Use dinner as a low-pressure meetup: choose a table together, compare orientation notes, and confirm Saturday’s meeting point.
cards.short_summary: The first shared meal anchors the weekend in Harvard’s first-year dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard Dining identifies Annenberg as a dining hall at Memorial Hall and restricts lunch and dinner to first-year students.
cards.access_notes: Lunch and dinner are limited to first-years. The current page lists daily dinner from 4:30–7:30 p.m.; academic-calendar closures may apply.

cards.title: Friday: Claim a Study Base
cards.subtitle: End the evening at 1 Harvard Yard
cards.notes: Test one quiet area and one collaborative area, then save the library contact details before the first full week begins.
cards.short_summary: An early introduction to Harvard’s round-the-clock humanities study hub.
cards.evidence_claim: Lamont offers quiet and collaborative study areas, media-production resources, and access for Harvard students, faculty, and staff.
cards.access_notes: A Harvard ID is required. Harvard describes Lamont as a 24-hour library, but displayed daily desk and service hours can be shorter.

cards.title: Saturday: Walk the Official Tour
cards.subtitle: Depart from the Harvard Visitor Center
cards.notes: Reserve ahead, arrive 15 minutes early at Smith Campus Center, and use the route to connect names on the map with real landmarks.
cards.short_summary: A student-led overview turns Harvard Yard into a usable mental map.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard’s free, student-led Historical Tour departs from the Smith Campus Center, explores Harvard Yard, and typically lasts 45–60 minutes.
cards.access_notes: Advance registration is required for the in-person tour; Harvard releases registration beginning the Friday before each tour week.

cards.title: Saturday: Browse the Art Museums
cards.subtitle: Choose one gallery thread to follow
cards.notes: Pick a theme or material before entering, compare three works as a group, and photograph only where current gallery rules allow.
cards.short_summary: A focused gallery prompt keeps a first museum visit conversational and manageable.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard states that the Harvard Art Museums are free and open to all visitors Tuesday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday through Sunday according to Harvard’s current museum overview; check the museum’s visit information for daily hours and closures.

cards.entity_name: Carpenter Center for the Visual Arts
cards.title: Saturday: Follow the Carpenter Center Ramp
cards.subtitle: Pair contemporary art with Le Corbusier’s building
cards.notes: Walk the exterior ramp, study how it frames the campus, then enter the galleries and compare the architecture with the current exhibition.
cards.short_summary: A compact stop combining contemporary exhibitions and a distinctive campus building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Carpenter Center is Harvard’s contemporary-art center, offers free public admission, and occupies Le Corbusier’s only North American building.
cards.source_title: Carpenter Center for the Visual Arts
cards.access_notes: The current official page lists public hours of noon–5 p.m., Thursday through Sunday; verify holiday or exhibition-change closures.

cards.title: Saturday: Regroup at the Plaza
cards.subtitle: Meet between the Science Center and Harvard Yard
cards.notes: Choose a visible landmark as your meetup point, scan the posted calendar, and use the outdoor seating for a group schedule check.
cards.short_summary: A central outdoor pause helps everyone reset before the evening disperses.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard identifies Science Center Plaza as a major campus crossroads used for markets, concerts, skating, and other activities.
cards.access_notes: The plaza is outdoors; specific events, concessions, and seasonal activities operate on their own schedules.

cards.title: Sunday: Take a Common Loop
cards.subtitle: Walk the city park outside Harvard Square
cards.notes: Follow the park pathways, identify one historic monument, and use a bench or lawn as the weekend’s quiet conversation break.
cards.short_summary: A relaxed outdoor loop adds Cambridge’s civic landscape to the campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Cambridge identifies Cambridge Common as a 16-acre city park and National Historic Landmark with lawns, monuments, and pathways.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor city park. Follow posted park rules and check city notices for temporary construction or event impacts.

cards.entity_name: Harvard Museum of the Ancient Near East
cards.title: Sunday: Close with Ancient Objects
cards.subtitle: Finish the sequence at a free museum
cards.notes: Choose one gallery, read the object labels closely, and each share a single detail worth remembering before leaving the weekend route.
cards.short_summary: A small, structured museum visit gives Sunday a calm and reflective finish.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harvard Museum of the Ancient Near East offers free admission and is open Sunday through Friday from 11 a.m.–4 p.m.
cards.source_title: Visit | Harvard Museum of the Ancient Near East
cards.access_notes: Current public hours are Sunday–Friday, 11 a.m.–4 p.m.; the museum lists specific holiday closures and occasional early closings.
